what: 1. 2026-06-16 to 19 — Method developed at the Lorentz Center workshop
title: Lab notebook
text: Context. Group D (Fanny Bergström, David Price, Nathalie Dean, Hein Putter, Kylie Ainslie) Lorentz Center workshop Connecting Survival Analysis Infectious Disease Modelling (Leiden, 15–19 June 2026). Aim: improve efficiency VE estimation using force infection experienced different subpopulations. Data. workshop case study: HERMES simulation 200,000 people generated organisers, provided demographic_data.rds, vaccination_data.rds incidence_data_reduced.rds. VE generating data known participants. Method developed (workshop repo, branch group-D, analysis/group-D/): data_wrangling.R: merge data, sample cohort 10,000, daily incidence age group vaccination status, counting-process data split vaccination, expansion person-days, prevalence reported cases (7-day infectious period starting 2 days reporting). prepare_stan_data.R: age-structured FoI ‾(tc,)=∑′Ca′aIa′eff(tc−1)/Na\bar (t_c, ) = \sum_{'} C_{'} ^{\text{eff}}_{'}(t_c - 1) / N_a using POLYMOD Netherlands contact matrix, plus overall-prevalence version; person-days aggregated cells. model.stan: Poisson approximation Cox model, log⁡μ=log⁡β+log⁡‾+log⁡D+γ(t)V\log\mu = \log\beta + \log\bar + \log D + \gamma(t)V, daily random walk γ(t)\gamma(t) γ(1)∼N(−1,1)\gamma(1) \sim N(-1, 1). run_model.R: fits age-structured overall-prevalence versions. analysis_Poisson_and_Cox.R (Hein Putter, 2026-06-19): frequentist Poisson Cox fits piecewise-constant hazard ratios. Check: parameter recovery simulated outcomes (simulate_validate.R, 2026-06-17). Event counts simulated model known log⁡β=−4.4\log\beta = -4.4 rise--wane γ(t)\gamma(t), keeping real covariate structure, refitted.  Results recorded workshop vignette: log⁡β\log\beta recovered accurately (true −4.4, posterior median −4.40). γ(t)\gamma(t) recovered well two weeks, flattened rapidly widening uncertainty. followed event sparsity vaccinated group (events near zero days 13–20), sampler failure. Earlier sampler problems fixed non-centred parameterisation (model_noncentered.stan). case-study data, VE rose 88% day 15, appeared plateau 70–72% day 45–90 (judged likely prior-driven), early dip −22% days 2–3 (plausibly reporting-delay effect). Notes added 2026-11-25. vignette states θ=0.5\theta = 0.5 (vaccinated cases half infectious), prepare_stan_data.R used theta <- 1 (vaccinated cases infectious ). scripts hard-coded study end (93 days one place, 90 another); see entry 6. case-study VE unknown, checks test model , known truth. motivated entry 2.

title: Lab notebook

Frequentist Poisson GLMs cells Stan model, one VE per range days since vaccination (piecewise constant): : one baseline + FoI offset (Stan model’s structure); B: separate baseline calendar day + FoI offset; C: separate baseline calendar day + age group, FoI (equivalent Cox model calendar time). Days cases dropped B C, since carry information day baseline. true VE per range mean vaccinated person-days. Script. dev/checks/2026-11-25_03_calendar_time.R (seconds; base R). Results (waning scenario, VE 90% CI): Case-weighted mean error day 90 : −0.22, B −0.10, C −0.08 (waning); 0.00, B +0.03, C +0.04 (waning, 3 vaccinated cases 90–119 days none 120+, 120+ estimable).  Observations. Model reproduces Stan model’s late error (−0.22), piecewise GLM fair stand-question. per-day baseline roughly halves late error. Earlier ranges barely change. remaining error (−0.1) well inside intervals (41 vaccinated cases day 90); one realisation separate chance. B C give almost identical estimates interval widths: day baseline, POLYMOD-based FoI adds nothing beyond age effect . may reflect POLYMOD contacts describe HERMES transmits (households, schools, workplaces). Relevant project’s premise FoI improves precision; worth revisiting FoI built simulation’s contact structure. Conclusion. Calendar-time confounding explains half late underestimate. code: library(surviver)  # person-level data: demographics, vaccination and reported cases pop <- ve_population(ve_sim_waning)  # force of infection by day and age group, from reported cases inc  <- daily_incidence(pop) prev <- daily_prevalence(inc, duration_infection = 7, reporting_delay = 2) foi  <- force_of_infection(prev, age_group_sizes(pop), contact_matrix = polymod_nl)  # person-days split at vaccination, aggregated for Stan pd <- expand_person_days(counting_process(pop)) sd <- make_stan_data(pd, foi)  # fit and plot against the true curve fit <- fit_ve(sd, seed = 42) ve  <- extract_ve(fit) plot_ve(ve, truth = ve_sim_waning$params)
